key_insight: The paper reports the first anhydrous, perfectly cubic Na$_2$IrCl$_6$ single crystals, filling a missing member of the $A_2$IrCl$_6$ vacancy-ordered iridate family and identifying them as a new $J_{eff}=1/2$ candidate with fcc antiferromagnetism.
engineering_relevance: This expands the design space for vacancy-ordered double perovskites by linking crystal chemistry, hydration control, and magnetic ground state, which is useful for studying spin-orbit-driven correlated materials and Kitaev-type interactions.
method: Use comprehensive structural and thermal characterization to confirm cubic phase and absence of lattice water.
Measure magnetic behavior to identify an antiferromagnetic transition at 1.91 K.
evidence_signal: Thermogravimetric analysis showed no lattice water and thermal stability up to 453 K, while magnetic measurements revealed an antiferromagnetic transition at 1.91 K.
watch_item: The key result depends on maintaining anhydrous cubic phase stability, so moisture sensitivity and possible hydration-driven structural changes remain a practical concern.
paper_title: Na$_2$Ir$^\text{IV}$Cl$_6$: The Missing Member of the Perfectly Cubic Vacancy Ordered $A_2$IrCl$_6$ Family, Another Potential $J_{eff}$ = $\frac{1}{2}$ Ground State Candidate
